The belfry has hung an empty shell for forty years, what left it has been growing in the lake — and at midnight it rings back, from under the water, answering its shell.

The midnight ringing is nearer the shore each week; fish beach in spirals; and the bellfounder's ledger — the NPC's inheritance, their father cast it — records the commission with a line the NPC can now read as confession: "to the pattern the visitor supplied."

It comes up the beach at midsummer wearing the lake, bronze and vast and patient, and re-hangs itself. Thereafter the town lives by true ringing: honest hours, honest tolling for every death including the upcoming ones — and once a year, a note that calls something else's children home, the way it was once called itself.
omen, family, truth

The NPC inherited the town's founding charter and read the boundary clause aloud to settle a property dispute — and the boundaries heard. The town's edges have begun enforcing themselves as written. They were written drunk, in the founding year, generously. — The town is legally four times its size and the land is complying: forest un-growing along the old ink-line, the barony's border-stones migrating at night, their garrison waking up inside "town limits" and subject to market law. The barony calls it invasion. The charter calls it Tuesday. — The barony sends soldiers — and the charter, read further in desperation, turns out to contain militia obligations, a wall clause, and a founding curse on "all who contest these bounds," all of which now also enforce themselves. The realm learns that written law, read aloud by the right blood, is load-bearing — and every chartered town locks its founding documents in iron. — authority, curse, home

The consultations are discreet — a hooded figure at the counter asking hypotheticals: whether a man who poisoned wells deserves the same hour as a midwife; what mercy owes the unrepentant — and the NPC has realized, with mounting horror, that their kitchen-table answers are being applied: the town's deaths have begun to carry a signature of considered timing, and the realm's priests have noticed the district where dying got gentle.

Death's consultations conclude and the revision publishes: the realm's deaths re-timed on principles one shopkeeper articulated over tea — gentler in the main, stranger at the edges, every deathbed now carrying the faint sense of having been scheduled by someone who thought about it — and the NPC lives out their days as the uncredited author of mortality's current edition, knowing exactly which clause they'd amend, and knowing Death knows their hour, and has promised, professionally, to bring the paperwork.
